subject: leafy seadragon
title: This Fish Looks Like Seaweed, and the Dad Carries 250 Eggs

scenes.text: This fish is covered in leaves, and none of them help it swim.
The leafy seadragon lives only off southern Australia and grows to about 14 inches.
Those leafy flaps are pure camouflage. It drifts like a loose piece of seaweed.
To move, it flutters tiny, almost see-through fins you can barely spot.
It has no teeth and no stomach. It sucks up tiny shrimp through its tube snout.
And the mom doesn't carry the babies. Dad holds up to 300 eggs under his tail for about two months.

description:
The leafy seadragon (Phycodurus eques) lives only in temperate southern Australia and reaches about 35 cm. Its leaf-like appendages are camouflage; it swims with small, nearly transparent dorsal and pectoral fins.
It has no teeth or stomach and sucks in tiny crustaceans. The male carries 250-300 eggs on the underside of his tail for 6-8 weeks.
Which camouflage animal fools you the most?
first_comment: Divers often swim right past them without noticing. Would you have spotted it?
